To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the super-tall buildings in Calm and windy climates have a significant impact on pedestrian wind comfort in the urban area and the effect of building configuration on pedestrian wind comfort depends on the incident wind direction and the climate condition.

the pedestrian level mean wind speeds in the urban area increase significantly after the construction of the super-tall buildings, and the area with pedestrian wind comforts decreases in both Windy and Cal climate.

the construction of a 400 m tall building at the center of an urban-like setting results in a significant reduction in pedestrian wind comfort for both Calm and Wind climates, and that minor aerodynamic modifications such windward setback, tapered and rounded shapes, as well as corner modifications, show promise in improving wind comfort for Calm and/or Windy climates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of the construction of a 400 m tall building in an urban-like context on pedestrian wind comfort.

the evaluation of pedestrian wind comfort near a single super-tall building located at the center an urban-like setting, and the results are useful to the design of super-tall buildings in urban areas.
the impact of a super-tall buildings on pedestrian wind comfort and provides insights on the design of super-tall buildings to mitigate wind discomfort in urban-like settings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the super-tall buildings with sharp corners, frontal area and plan aspect ratio, and the ones with large plan aspect ratio are more likely to cause wind problems in both Calm and Wind climates.
the pedestrian wind comfort near a high-rise building is a function of building configuration and ambient wind speed.
the pedestrian wind comfort near a tall building depends on the building configuration, incident wind direction and the ambient wind speed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a square-shaped super tall building with sharp corners, plan aspect ratios, and frontal areas would be a poor candidate in terms of pedestrian wind comfort, especially for Windy climates.
a super-tall square-shaped building is not recommended in Calm and/or Windy climate, especially when the orientation is perpendicular to the prevailing wind direction.
the construction of a 400 m tall building in an urban area is not recommended unless it is aerodynamically shaped and located in the right place.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the super-tall buildings should be carefully located and designed, especially with respect to the incident wind direction and building shape to minimize the impact on pedestrian wind comfort in the urban area.
the super-tall buildings should be designed to reduce the impact of wind loads in the urban area.
the super-tall buildings with sharp corners and large frontal areas should be designed with care to avoid adverse effects on wind comfort.
